verdict.rationale: USCIS publishes its delegation form and the roles it covers. Form G-28 must be submitted by an attorney or accredited representative to represent a client, and representatives can file on a client's behalf and submit later G-28s through a representative online account. The evidence does not say what a third party may not do or which signatures must remain the applicant's own. Missing for 10: published limits on representative actions, rules on which signatures stay personal to the applicant, any role beyond attorney/accredited representative (e.g., preparers), independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, exactly what a third party may and may not do on my behalf is published — the authorization forms, the roles, and which signatures stay personal

citations.quote: An attorney or accredited representative must submit Form G-28, Notice of Entry of Appearance as Attorney or Accredited Representative, to establish eligibility to represent a client in an immigration matter before USCIS.
To file a form online on behalf of your client, along with Form G-28, you must first create a USCIS online account.
You can submit subsequent Forms G-28 online for certain pending forms. In your USCIS representative online account, navigate to File a Form, and choose Form G-28
